diagnosis.what_happened: Chapter 4 compilation to docx resulted in Arabic Naskh fallback for Persian text, unisolated Latin acronyms, AI clichés in text, and unlocalized numerals.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Missing OpenXML attributes (w:hint="cs", w:eastAsia) in python-docx generator and lack of regex parsing/prompt sanitization in drafting stage.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Persian text should be explicitly typed with OpenXML attributes preventing fallback, Latin acronyms isolated in Times New Roman, numerals converted to Persian, and text sanitized from AI clichés.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Proper typographic standards are required for Persian academic documents to ensure visual consistency and adherence to university formatting guidelines.

desired_behavior: Modify python-docx compiler to inject w:hint="cs" and w:eastAsia into w:rFonts for Persian text. Enforce regex parsing for Latin acronym isolation. Sanitize markdown generation from AI clichés. Localize all numbers to Persian digits.
generalization: All OpenXML generation for Persian academic texts must explicitly define language hints to prevent Arabic fallback, and enforce strict typography for Latin scripts and numerals.

evidence.observed_value: Missing w:hint="cs" and unisolated Latin text
evidence.threshold_value: Strict OpenXML attribute presence and text sanitization
